_meta.description: Machine-readable prioritized action list derived from maturity-gap-dashboard.md. Each item corresponds to a confirmed or strongly-inferred gap with evidence links.

priorityLevels.P0: Blocker - simulator produces wrong results or HDL export is unparseable. Fix before any non-trivial use.
priorityLevels.P1: High - correctness risk or missing safety net. Fix before production or teaching use.
priorityLevels.P2: Medium - completeness, coverage, or documentation. Address incrementally.

items.title: FSM export projection semantics missing for STT and timing
items.resolutionNote: The FSM0 current scope is now closed. Projection metadata, shared batch semantics, static/reduced STT core helpers, clean/legacy/modified/mixed semantics, shared STT/timing panel state, early editor/canvas guardrails, and the fixture-backed boundary wall for projected+raw, chained, observer, mixed-islands, shared-observer, and shared-helper cases are implemented and verified. Remaining follow-up is consciously deferred to FSM0-8 (Netzlisten-Minimierung / Bool-Minimierung / Mapping), not further current-scope projection groundwork.
evidence: validation/fsm0/work-package.md: current-scope closure with Abschlussbewertung and fixture-backed boundary wall

items.symptom: FSMs synthesized from the FSM editor can be functionally correct on canvas and in HDL export, but the remaining mixed and wide cases still need a fully deterministic projection layer. Without the final reduction and fallback rules, STT and timing can still drift back toward raw gate/helper networks in edge cases.
items.recommendedNextStep: No further current-scope action required. If the FSM strand is reopened, restart deliberately with FSM0-8: Netzlisten-Minimierung / Bool-Minimierung / Mapping for broad synthesis, plus optional additional legacy breadth if needed.
items.riskIfUnfixed: N/A - current scope closed. Residual future value lies in minimization and optional broader fixture breadth, not unresolved current-scope projection inconsistency.

items.title: Race panel lifecycle semantics missing for reset, pruning, and dedupe
evidence: validation/race-panel-fixes/work-package.md: documented requirements plus the first implemented/verifizierter lifecycle slice
src/store/raceLifecycle.ts: central race signature, prune, dedupe, and active-net helpers
src/store/CircuitContext.tsx: store-side append dedupe, structure-prune effect, and clearRaceMonitor() reset path
src/components/panels/RacePanel.tsx: panel exposes Monitor reset and focuses the first still-existing affected gate
src/__tests__/core/raceLifecycle.test.ts: helper regressions for dedupe, signature stability, prune, and max-limit behavior
items.symptom: Before the first lifecycle slice, stale race incidents could survive structural deletes, the panel had no manual reset path, and repeated identical race detections could keep filling the incident list. A first store-side fix now addresses the core UX failures, but deeper incident semantics and integration coverage are still open.
affectedGates: all circuits that can emit race or hazard incidents in gate-delay mode
items.recommendedNextStep: Build on the implemented first slice in validation/race-panel-fixes/work-package.md: keep the store-side lifecycle helpers, then add deeper incident metadata/integration coverage and decide whether manual reset should remain a pure clear action or gain optional short-term suppression semantics for still-active hazards.
items.riskIfUnfixed: Without the remaining integration hardening, the race monitor can still regress toward a noisy event log instead of a robust incident monitor. Future UI or scheduler changes could silently weaken prune/reset semantics without deeper coverage.
items.partialResolutionNote: First slice implemented and verified: store-side pruning removes stale incidents when affected nets or all referenced gates disappear, clearRaceMonitor() clears panel state and wire markings through a single central path, repeated identical incidents are coalesced by normalized signature, and RacePanel exposes an explicit manual reset button. Remaining work is narrower: deeper incident metadata, integration tests around provider/reset paths, and any future policy about immediate rediscovery of still-active hazards after a manual reset.

summary.note: All P0 blockers and P1-1 through P1-7 remain resolved. As of 2026-03-22, Contract Runner v1 is operational at 447 pass, 0 fail, 0 unsupported; Golden Corpus v1 is operational at 28 pass, 0 fail, 2 expected_limit across 30 circuits with live export-determinism plus external HDL syntax/lint and scenario-based simulation enabled. Focused-Nine UI audit remains a CI gate (12 smoke PASS, 5 semantic PASS). CI has 6 jobs. Current investment areas: canonical FSM export projection semantics, structured race-panel lifecycle semantics, Golden Corpus acceptance/report hardening, branch protection, CI performance, and deeper hierarchy/custom-IC verification.
